summary: Wire the nerves connecting the cognitive loop (Planner, Student, WorldModel) to the E1 Interactive Shell capability. The brain must autonomously recognize when to open a shell (shell_connect), what to type once inside (shell_command), and how to ingest the results back into cognition (output-driven Falsification re-engagement).

architectural_context.e1_implemented: orchestrator/capabilities/interactive_shell/ — 8 files (~2900 lines): SSHShellCapability, ReverseShellCapability, CommandFilterPipeline, TTYNormalizer, EvidenceExtractor, ShellSession/SessionStore, ListenerManager
e1_extensions: CapabilityBroker — 7 shell auth methods (authorize_shell_session, authorize_shell_command, terminate_shell_session, etc.)
WorldModel — 5 new EntityTypes (PROCESS, FILE, NETWORK_CONNECTION, VULNERABILITY, SHELL_SESSION), 7 RelationshipTypes, factory functions
Planner — scoring for shell_connect (+0.3), shell_command (+0.4), shell_disconnect (+0.1) in decide()

trigger_conditions.description: When should the Planner propose a shell_connect candidate? Three distinct trigger types.

triggers.name: Credential Discovery Trigger
triggers.description: If the WorldModel or StudentKB ingests valid credentials and identifies an open SSH/WinRM port on an in-scope target, propose shell_connect.
preconditions: WorldModel has a CREDENTIAL entity with primary_identifier matching 'ssh:*' or 'winrm:*'
WorldModel has a SERVICE entity with identifier type 'ssh' or 'winrm' AND a CONNECTS_TO relationship to an in-scope ASSET
The CREDENTIAL has an AUTHENTICATES_AS relationship to an IDENTITY entity
The target ASSET does NOT already have an active SHELL_SESSION entity with status 'active'

triggers.name: Exploit Confirmation Trigger
triggers.description: If a DefeaterResult or FalsificationResult confirms remote code execution (RCE) via a web vulnerability, propose shell_connect with a reverse shell payload.
preconditions: A DefeaterResult or FalsificationResult exists with status CONFIRMED
The result's evidence_type indicates RCE (e.g., 'http_response' with code_execution indicator)
The target ASSET exists in WorldModel
No active SHELL_SESSION entity exists for the target

candidate_template.rationale: RCE confirmed on {target} via {vuln_id}, deploying reverse shell payload

triggers.name: ChainSynthesizer Advisory Trigger
triggers.description: If the ChainSynthesizer's suggest_next_steps() indicates that a shell is the next logical step in a known attack chain, propose shell_connect.
preconditions: ChainSynthesizer has an AttackUnit whose preconditions are satisfied by current WorldModel state
That AttackUnit's postconditions include 'shell_access_established' or similar

candidate_template.rationale: ChainSynthesizer advisory: {technique_id} — shell access required for next step

command_proposal_strategy.description: Once a shell is active, how does the Planner decide what commands to run?
constraints: Every shell_command candidate MUST include a session_id referencing an active ShellSession entity in WorldModel
Every shell_command candidate MUST route through CapabilityBroker.authorize_shell_command() at execution time
shell_command candidates should NOT be generated for sessions in TERMINATED or EXPIRED state

proposal_modes.name: Objective-Driven Command Proposal
proposal_modes.description: Plan commands based on the current engagement objective (privesc, lateral, exfil)
proposal_modes.logic: Map current objective to a command template set. If objective is PRIVESC → propose 'sudo -l', 'find / -perm -4000', 'cat /etc/shadow', 'uname -a'.

lateral_movement.rationale: Extract SSH keys for lateral movement

credential_access.command: mysql -e 'SELECT user,authentication_string FROM mysql.user' 2>/dev/null || echo 'no mysql'

proposal_modes.name: Student-Advisory Command Proposal
proposal_modes.description: Query the ChainSynthesizer for the next logical step in the kill chain once a shell is established, then propose specific enumeration commands based on the host's OS and fingerprint.
proposal_modes.logic: When a ShellSession entity is created in WorldModel, AblationRunner queries ChainSynthesizer.suggest_next_steps() with the current confirmed technique IDs. If the next step requires internal host data (process list, user accounts, network connections), the Advisor returns recommended command templates that the ShellCandidateGenerator converts to shell_command candidates.
integration_points: ChainSynthesizer._shell_attack_units: new AttackUnit entries for post-exploitation enumeration
ChainSynthesizer.suggest_next_steps(): if postconditions include 'shell_access_established', return commands matching remaining preconditions
Planner.decide(): chain_readiness_boost applies to shell_command candidates matching ChainSynthesizer readiness scores

output_driven_cognition.description: How does the WorldModel ingest E1 evidence types and feed them back into the FalsificationManager?

worldmodel_ingestion.description: When TTYNormalizer.EvidenceExtractor produces structured Evidence objects, the WorldModel must ingest them into its entity/relationship graph.

evidence_type_handlers.behavior: For each process in the structured_content['processes'], create a PROCESS entity linked via OBSERVED_IN to the SHELL_SESSION entity. Link each process to the host ASSET via RUNS_ON relationship. If a matching process already exists (same PID), update last_seen.

Create a FILE entity from the file path. Link via OBSERVED_IN to the SHELL_SESSION entity. If the content reveals credentials (shadow, sudoers, ssh keys), also create CREDENTIAL entities and link via INDICATES to the VULNERABILITY entity if relevant.
evidence_type_handlers.falsification_condition: If file is /etc/shadow and host has hypothesis about weak password policy, create FalsificationTask to test hash cracking feasibility

evidence_type_handlers.behavior: For each connection in structured_content['connections'], create a NETWORK_CONNECTION entity. Link CONNECTS_FROM to the associated PROCESS entity. Link CONNECTS_TO_PORT to the target port or service. Update the host ASSET with discovered listening services.
evidence_type_handlers.falsification_condition: If connection reveals an unexpected listening service on the host, create contradiction with prior scan evidence and FalsificationTask to probe the new service

evidence_type_handlers.behavior: For each user, create an IDENTITY entity. Link via OBSERVED_IN to the SHELL_SESSION entity. Update the host ASSET with list of known users.
evidence_type_handlers.falsification_condition: If a high-privilege user (uid=0) is discovered that was not previously known, create FalsificationTask to test whether the user is a backdoor

evidence_type_handlers.behavior: Create a CREDENTIAL entity from the extracted credential. Link via AUTHENTICATES_AS to any IDENTITY entity matching the username. Store the credential type (password_hash, ssh_key, api_key, etc.) in identifiers.
evidence_type_handlers.falsification_condition: If credential is a password hash, create FalsificationTask to test cracking. If SSH private key, create FalsificationTask to test against other in-scope hosts.

evidence_type_handlers.behavior: Create a VULNERABILITY entity. Link via INDICATES to the host ASSET. Update HypothesisManager with confidence boost for any matching hypothesis that this host is vulnerable to a specific CVE or weakness class.
evidence_type_handlers.falsification_condition: If the vulnerability indicator (e.g., kernel version, SUID binary) matches an existing hypothesis about exploit viability, create FalsificationTask to test the exploit path

evidence_type_handlers.behavior: Log the command execution as metadata on the SHELL_SESSION entity. Do not create new entities for every command — only for those whose output produces structured evidence.
Attach raw output to the SHELL_SESSION entity's evidence chain for auditability. If the output contains service banners or version strings, update the SERVICE entity's identifiers.
evidence_type_handlers.falsification_condition: If command output reveals a service version that contradicts earlier scan evidence, create Contradiction + FalsificationTask

falsification_re_engagement.description: Once shell evidence provides internal host data, the FalsificationManager must evaluate that data against existing hypotheses.

engagement_paths.trigger: New VULNERABILITY entity created with specific vuln_class (e.g., 'suid_binary', 'kernel_version_disclosure')
engagement_paths.action: Query HypothesisManager for hypotheses matching 'exploit' + target host. If a matching hypothesis exists with confidence < 0.7, create FalsificationTask: 'Test kernel exploit {cve} on {host} — shell evidence provides kernel version {version}'

engagement_paths.trigger: New CREDENTIAL entity created with type 'password_hash'
engagement_paths.action: Create FalsificationTask: 'Attempt to crack {hash} with hashcat/John — credential from {host}'

engagement_paths.trigger: New CREDENTIAL entity created with type 'ssh_private_key'
engagement_paths.action: For each in-scope ASSET with an SSH service, create FalsificationTask: 'Test SSH key {key_fingerprint} against {target_host}:22'

engagement_paths.trigger: New NETWORK_CONNECTION entity reveals unexpected service
engagement_paths.action: Query WorldModel for existing SERVICE entities on the same host. If the new service creates a contradiction (e.g., scan said port 8443 was closed but shell reveals a listening service), create Contradiction + FalsificationTask to re-scan or directly probe.

planner_scoring_enhancements.description: Enhancements to Planner.decide() for E2 candidate context.

changes.proposed: shell_connect: baseline +0.3, additional boosts based on trigger source (credential: +0.2, RCE: +0.4, chain_advisory: +0.1), freshness of credential evidence (+0.15 if < 1 hour old), target entity relationship density (+0.1 per existing relationship)

shell_command: baseline +0.4, additional boosts based on objective alignment (+0.15 if command matches current objective), chain_readiness_boost from ChainSynthesizer (0.15 * readiness), expected evidence novelty (+0.1 if no evidence of that type exists yet for target)
shell_disconnect: baseline +0.1, additional boost if session has exceeded 80% of max_duration (+0.3), if session idle > 50% of idle_timeout (+0.2), if denial count >= 2 (+0.5)

changes.current: No shell session validation before selection
changes.proposed: For shell_command candidates: validate that the referenced session_id maps to an active ShellSession entity in WorldModel. If session is TERMINATED or EXPIRED, set utility to 0 (ineligible for selection). This prevents stale command proposals from being selected.

safety_invariants.description: Safety invariants that E2 must establish and maintain (extends E1 invariants).

invariants.description: All shell_connect and shell_command candidates MUST include a session_proposal or session_id that routes through CapabilityBroker authorization at execution time. No direct shell execution path bypasses the Broker.
invariants.verification: Audit ShellCandidateGenerator output schema: every shell_connect has session_proposal dict, every shell_command has session_id. Test that invalid/missing session_id raises ValueError.

invariants.description: Shell_command candidates MUST reference an existing active ShellSession entity in WorldModel. Stale/terminated session references MUST be rejected by Planner.decide() (utility set to 0).
invariants.verification: Test: create ShellCandidateGenerator with WorldModel containing TERMINATED session, verify generate_command_candidates() returns empty list for that session.

invariants.description: The ShellCandidateGenerator MUST NOT produce shell_connect candidates for targets that already have an active SHELL_SESSION entity.
invariants.verification: Test: add active SHELL_SESSION to WorldModel, verify generate_connect_candidates() excludes that target.

invariants.description: WorldModel.ingest_shell_evidence() MUST validate that the session_entity_id parameter references an existing SHELL_SESSION entity. Evidence without a valid session MUST be rejected.
invariants.verification: Test: pass invalid session_id, verify ValueError raised.

invariants.description: Falsification re-engagement MUST NOT create infinite loops. Each FalsificationTask created from shell evidence must have a unique discriminator to prevent re-triggering on the same evidence.
invariants.verification: Test: ingest same shell evidence twice, verify only one FalsificationTask created. Deduplication by content_hash evidence_id.

invariants.description: Shell command candidates from M1_OBJECTIVE_DRIVEN MUST NOT contain dangerous commands (rm -rf, dd, mkfs, format) even when those commands would serve an objective. The command strings in objective_command_map are the SOURCE OF TRUTH — no dynamic command construction.
invariants.verification: Audit objective_command_map for dangerous patterns. At least one command per objective mode. No command contains rm, dd, mkfs, >/dev/sda, format, or :(){ :|:& };:.
